55: type statusRecorder struct {
56: 	http.ResponseWriter
57: 	code int
58: }
59: 
60: func (r *statusRecorder) Written() bool {
61: 	return r.code != 0
62: }
63: 
64: func (r *statusRecorder) WriteHeader(code int) {
65: 	r.code = code
66: 	r.ResponseWriter.WriteHeader(code)
67: }
68: 
69: func (r *statusRecorder) Status() int {
70: 	if r.code == 0 {
71: 		return http.StatusOK
72: 	}
73: 	return r.code
74: }
75: 
76: func (r *statusRecorder) Flush() {
77: 	if flusher, ok := r.ResponseWriter.(http.Flusher); ok {
78: 		flusher.Flush()
79: 	}
80: }

82: // Event is a string that represents the type of event being sent to the
83: // client. It is used in the Server-Sent Events (SSE) protocol to identify
84: // the type of data being sent.
85: // The client (template) will use this type in the sse event listener to
86: // determine how to handle the incoming data. It will also be used in the
87: // sse-swap htmx event listener to determine how to handle the incoming data.
88: type Event string

91: 	EventChat       Event = "chat"
92: 	EventComplete   Event = "complete"
93: 	EventLoading    Event = "loading"
94: 	EventToolResult Event = "tool_result" // Used for both tool calls and their results
95: 	EventThinking   Event = "thinking"
96: 	EventToolCall   Event = "tool_call"
